citation: Arens, S. A., Stoker, G., Barker, J., Shebby, S., Wang, X., Cicchinelli, L. F., & Williams, J. M. (2012). Effects of curriculum and teacher professional development on the language proficiency of elementary English language learner students in the Central Region. Final Report (NCEE 2012-4013). Washington, DC: U.S. Department of Education, Institute of Education Sciences, National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Regional Educational Laboratory Central, administered by Mid-continent Research for Education and Learning.
design: Cluster RCT; assignment level = School (2:1 allocation); 52 schools analyzed (34 intervention, 18 control) across Colorado, Kansas, Nebraska; intervention = 'On Our Way to English' (OWE) ELL curriculum + 'Responsive Instruction for Success in English' (RISE) teacher professional development vs business-as-usual ESL instruction; subject = English language proficiency/literacy for native Spanish-speaking ELL students; grades 1-5 (curriculum K-5).
problems: The report standardized the IPT outcome to z-scores and reports the impact in standardized (z-score) units (gamma01 = -0.03, SE = 0.06) plus a matching Glass's Delta effect size of -0.03; it does NOT report Hedges' g. The report explicitly chose Glass's Delta over Hedges' g (p.31), reasoning that the intervention could change the treatment-group SD. The unadjusted posttest SDs (0.84 intervention, 0.86 control) are very close to 1.0 because scores were z-standardized, so d via Glass's Delta (control-SD standardization) and d via the z-scored impact coefficient coincide at -0.03. Single dual intervention arm (OWE+RISE combined); the study was not designed to separate curriculum vs PD effects. Confirmatory outcome is non-significant (p=.66).

effect_sizes.arm_label: OWE curriculum + RISE teacher professional development (combined dual intervention) vs business-as-usual ESL
effect_sizes.test_name: IDEA Proficiency Test (IPT) basic composite score (listening comprehension + reading/vocabulary comprehension + writing)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (spring 2010, end of Year 2 implementation year)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported standardized HLM impact taken directly: gamma01 = -0.03, SE = 0.06 on z-scored IPT composite (Table 4.1, p.44; Table J2, p.J-2). This equals d because the outcome was already z-standardized; the report's own Glass's Delta = -0.03 (control-SD standardization) confirms d = -0.03. Hedges' g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2610, J = 0.99971; g = 0.99971*(-0.03) = -0.02999; g_se = J*0.06 = 0.05998; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.0035979.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 4.1 (p.44) confirmatory impact; Table J2 (p.J-2) full model; ICC from Table I1 (p.I-1); design/sample from Summary pp.xi-xii and Table 2.6/2.7
effect_sizes.notes: Confirmatory (headline) research question outcome: combined OWE+RISE impact on IPT basic composite. Two-level HLM (students nested in schools) adjusting for IPT pretest, percent White, percent Hispanic, block (district) randomization indicators, and student grade; intent-to-treat over 52 schools; multilevel model accounts for clustering so cluster_adjusted=true. ICC = 0.12 (Table I1). mean_t/mean_c are the adjusted IPT posttest means (intervention 0.00 -> reported -0.04 unadjusted; here adjusted means from Table 4.1: 0.00 vs 0.03); SDs (square brackets in Table 4.1) are unadjusted-posttest SDs of the z-scored composite (0.84 intervention, 0.86 control). Not statistically significant (p=.66, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.09). Subscale impacts (Models 6-8, Table 4.2): listening -0.02, reading -0.06, writing -0.03 (all NS); these are sensitivity/subscale analyses of the same composite and are NOT extracted as separate rows (composite is the confirmatory outcome). Sensitivity models (3-10) all NS, range -0.01 to -0.12.
